issues.issue: The name of the Q3 horizon fallback label, DEPENDS ON D INIT, makes a causal claim about D that the rule does not test. The rule fires whenever the three per-arm labels disagree and are not all negative. Seed noise alone often causes that disagreement, even when all three arms have the same distribution (which the init probe suggests for unit vs zero, see the next issue). The label is therefore often the modal horizon outcome in cases where D has no effect. It can also contradict the Q2 labels printed beside it, for example Q2 EQUIVALENT for both contrasts next to Q3 DEPENDS ON D INIT. This does not make any verdict unreachable. It does make the label wrong as worded in many plausible cases.
issues.evidence: Monte Carlo of the §7 rules as written: 20k reps, n=5, Welch-Satterthwaite, one-sided 95% L and 97.5% U, three TFPS arms iid (D irrelevant), sd_PatchTST 0.004, sd_DLinear 0.0015, shared baseline samples. P(DEPENDS ON D INIT) with identical arms: H=192, true gain m/2, sd_T 0.006: 0.60; sd_T 0.012: 0.75; true gain m, sd_T 0.012: 0.76. H=336, true gain 0, sd_T 0.012: 0.75 (single-arm VANISHES 0.53, INCONCLUSIVE 0.40). Script: scratchpad mc.py, re-runnable in about 10 s.
issues.fix: Rename the fallback to a neutral `NOT CONSISTENT ACROSS TFPS ARMS (gauss: ..., unit: ..., zero: ...)`. Add: 'if both Q2 contrasts at this H are labelled EQUIVALENT or INCONCLUSIVE, append "— Q2 detects no D effect; arm disagreement may be seed noise"'. Owner decision 9 is untouched: a negative still needs every arm.

issues.issue: tfps_gauss_unit is, at init, indistinguishable in routing from tfps_zero. Q2 for that contrast is therefore expected, though not guaranteed by construction, to give EQUIVALENT (if sd allows) or INCONCLUSIVE, with about 5% per side for rules 1-2 under a null. The prereg's stated init numbers for this arm are also off. Two exact facts follow from Cluster.py:61-68. (a) s_unit(z) = s_N01(z/sqrt(112)) for the same G, so the unit arm reaches the N(0,1) arm's init spread only if ||z|| grows about 10.6x (the s range of a random-subspace D is bounded near 0.14 at any scale; r2 sweep). (b) argmax s is scale-invariant, so at init arms 1 and 2 have the same argmax partition, and the Q2b noise-off unit model starts from the same deterministic routing as arm 1. The outcome stays open: training can grow z or rotate D through the KL term. This is not blocking, because Q2 asks whether the init matters in the released code, and 'no' is a legitimate answer. But a reader should know in advance that the unit arm is effectively a second random-routing control unless training sharpens s, and that the routing suffix will almost surely fire for it.

issues.issue: Reachability of the Q2 ', smaller than m_H' sub-labels is misstated. They use the 90% two-sided Q2 CI, so the floor is 2*hw_90 < m_H, i.e. sigma < m_H/2.352 at n=5 (0.0047 at H=192, 0.0021 at H=336). The prereg instead lumps them with SHRINKS under hw_L+hw_U, i.e. m/2.635. The stated floor is too strict by about 12%.
issues.evidence: PREREG l.179-180 (sub-labels on the 90% CI) vs l.227-228. Welch df 8: t.95 = 1.860, se = 0.632*sigma, hw = 1.176*sigma.
issues.fix: At l.227, split the sentence: 'Q2 ", smaller than m_H": 2·hw < m_H → σ < m_H/2.352 (0.0047 / 0.0021 at n=5; m_H/1.55 at n=10)'.

answers.q1_unit_vs_zero_routing: At init the two are not distinguishable. A is 0.2516/0.2505 for unit vs 0.2500 for zero, a gap of less than 1 noise-draw sd. The mean s range is 0.005/0.008 for unit vs 0 for zero. Q2(unit) is expected, not guaranteed, to come out EQUIVALENT or INCONCLUSIVE. It can differ only if training grows ||z|| by about 10x or the KL term rotates D. The routing suffix (A < 0.30) will almost surely fire for unit.
answers.q2_horizon_rule: Negative horizon labels are reachable, and including tfps_zero does not make them unreachable. Per-arm labels are strongly correlated because all three arms share the same baseline samples. With identical arms and no true gain, VANISHES (or worse) fires at the horizon level 0.86-0.96 at H=192 and 0.88-0.96 at H=336 for sd_T ≤ 0.006, close to the single-arm rate. Negatives become rare only when the zero arm is truly better (H=336, sd_T 0.012: 0.06), or when noise is large (H=336, sd_T 0.012: 0.18 vs single-arm 0.53). The real cost of the rule falls on SURVIVES, which needs unanimity (0.14-0.24 vs 0.51-0.61 for a single arm at sd_T 0.012), and on the over-frequent DEPENDS ON D INIT label (major issue above).
answers.q3_reachability_numbers: Recomputed, all correct. n=5 equal sd: df 8, t 1.860/2.306, hw_L 1.176σ, hw_U 1.458σ. sd ratio 0.1: df 4.08, hw_L 0.956σ_T, hw_U 1.243σ_T (prereg 0.953/1.238, a negligible difference). n=10: df 18, 0.775σ/0.940σ. Q2 EQUIVALENT: 0.0094/0.0043 (n=5), 0.0142/0.0064 (n=10). SHRINKS: PatchTST 0.0140/0.0049, DLinear 0.0042/0.0057 (n=5). The 'no width floor' claim for REVERSED/VANISHES/SURVIVES/Q2 rules 1-2 is literally true. VANISHES needs U in [0, m) because REVERSED is checked first, a window of width m in d. Exceptions: the Q2 sub-label and Q2b floors (minor issues). For the DLinear contrast in the realistic unequal-sd case, the SHRINKS floor is σ_T < 0.011/2.199 = 0.0050 at H=192.

summary: No verdict family is settled or made unreachable by how the arms are built. The forward probe shows that tfps_gauss_unit routing at init matches tfps_zero (A 0.2516/0.2505 vs 0.2500; mean s range 0.005/0.008), because s_unit(z) = s_N01(z/√112). Q2(unit) is therefore expected, though not guaranteed, to come out EQUIVALENT or INCONCLUSIVE, and §5's init numbers for that arm should be corrected. The all-arms rule for negative Q3 labels does not make them unreachable: shared baselines keep the arm labels correlated (VANISHES at the horizon level 0.86-0.96 under a no-gain null). But DEPENDS ON D INIT fires 60-80% with identical arms, so it needs a neutral name (major, mechanical fix). The §7 reachability numbers are correct, except for the Q2 sub-label and Q2b paired floors.
